purpose: Define each `#CAL` schedule as a stable declarative temporal identity separate from its next occurrence, emitted Event, Trigger binding and downstream execution.

topics.name: Schedule Identity
topics.purpose: Define each `#CAL` schedule as a stable declarative temporal identity separate from its next occurrence, emitted Event, Trigger binding and downstream execution.

semantics.identity_rule: Every machine-significant schedule has an explicit stable canonical identity.
semantics.definition_rule: Schedule definition contains temporal recurrence/occurrence semantics only.
semantics.occurrence_rule: Each concrete scheduled occurrence has its own occurrence identity/time evidence.
semantics.event_rule: Occurrence may emit an explicit scheduling Event; Event identity is distinct from schedule identity.
semantics.trigger_rule: Trigger binding is a separate explicit relation.
semantics.execution_rule: Schedule never directly owns or performs Runner/command execution.
semantics.state_rule: configured/enabled/paused/expired runtime states are separate from canonical schedule identity.
semantics.authority_rule: Schedule existence/visibility grants no downstream execution authority.

invariants.rule: A schedule determines when a scheduling occurrence may be emitted; it never directly executes a Routine, command or operation. Execution requires the normal explicit Event→Trigger→Runner/operation causality chain.

hard_gates.condition: schedule identity reused as Event identity
runtime paused state rewrites canonical identity
